बड़ी खुशखबरी! रिलीज से सिर्फ पांच दिन पहले Ramayana की एडवांस बुकिंग ने ₹40 करोड़ का आंकड़ा पार कर दिया है। 🔥
नितीश तिवारी के निर्देशन में बनी इस फिल्म का वर्ल्ड प्रीमियर इस हफ्ते लॉस एंजिल्स में हुआ था, जिसके बाद अमेरिका में प्री-सेल्स में जबरदस्त उछाल आया है। 🎬
भारत में डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर Dharma Productions और एग्जिबिटर्स के बीच रेवेन्यू शेयर को लेकर डेडलॉक चल रहा था, जिसकी वजह से कई शोज नहीं खुले थे।
डिस्ट्रीब्यूटर की मांग थी कि पहले 11 दिनों में 55% शेयर मिले या फिर थ्री-वीक स्लैब स्ट्रक्चर हो, लेकिन एग्जिबिटर्स अपने कॉस्ट की जिम्मेदारी का हवाला देकर ज्यादा रेवेन्यू देने को तैयार नहीं थे। 🤝
Sacnilk की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक शुक्रवार को यह डेडलॉक सुलझ गया, हालांकि दोनों पक्षों ने तय की गई सटीक शर्तों को साझा नहीं किया है।
शनिवार तक फिल्म के लिए स्क्रीन्स की संख्या बढ़कर लगभग 2500 हो गई और 31 अक्टूबर की दोपहर तक भारत में एडवांस बुकिंग ₹16.5 करोड़ हो गई, जिसमें 3 लाख से ज्यादा टिकट बिके।
विदेशी एडवांस बुकिंग में फिल्म ने $2.5 मिलियन की कमाई कर ली है, जिसमें अमेरिका के पेड प्रीव्यू के लिए $1 million शामिल हैं।
फिल्म में Ranbir Kapoor भगवान राम के रूप में, Sai Pallavi सीता के रूप में और Yash रावण के रूप में नजर आएंगे। 🌟
क्या आपने Ramayana की एडवांस बुकिंग के लिए टिकट बुक किया या नहीं? नीचे कमेंट्स में बताओ! 👇

ctx.title: Ramayana advance booking crosses  ₹40 crore five days before release; deadlock with Indian exhibitors ends for Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film
ctx.summary: Ramayana is set to have a global release on November 5, preceded by paid previews in North America on November 4 evening.
ctx.text:
The floodgates have opened for Ramayana advance booking with less than a week to go for its big release. The Nitesh Tiwari film had its world premiere in Los Angeles earlier this week, which led to a huge jump in pre-sales in the US. But back home, the film had been crippled by a deadlock between the distributors and exhibitors, due to which many shows hadn’t opened up. On Saturday, the deadlock was finally broken, raising hopes for an increased pace of advance bookings in its final week.
Advance bookings for Ramayana opened on Dussehra, 15 full days before its global release. But for the next 10 days, only the Hindi version had extensive shows. And there, too, most of the single-screen and smaller centres had yet to open. The reason was a stalemate between the distributors and exhibitors. Dharma Productions, the film’s distributor in India, had asked for a higher share of theatrical revenue, citing the film's higher production costs. The distributors had shared two options: a 55% share over the first 11 days, or a three-week slab structure, with 60% going to the distributor in week 1, 50% in week 2, and 40% in week 3. The exhibitors were unwilling to give up higher revenue as they said they were responsible for their costs. Additionally, they were wary of setting a precedent, as a settlement could prompt other big films to seek higher revenue.
This led to a stalemate, with negotiations continuing for over a week. Sacnilk reported that on Friday, the deadlock was resolved, even though neither party shared the exact terms agreed upon. By Saturday, the number of screens for the film had increased to almost 2500. By October 31 afternoon, five days before its release, the film had grossed ₹ 16.5 crore in advance bookings in India, selling over 3 lakh tickets. The Kannada version, which had been limited to a handful of shows, now accounted for 13% of the total gross across 150 screens. The Telugu and Tamil shows are also opening up steadily now and should be fully open by Monday.
A post shared by Ramayana: Rise of a Legend (@ramayanamovie)
What has helped Ramayana’s case is the pre-sales buzz overseas. In North America, the film will have paid previews on November 4, the eve of its release. The 24 hours after its world premiere saw the film register a 27% jump in collections. By Friday, the film had earned $2.5 million in overseas advance bookings, including over $1 million for the US paid previews alone. This takes the film’s worldwide advance-booking gross to ₹ 40 crore five days before its release.
Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus Studios in collaboration with DNEG and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, Ramayana is planned as a two-part film. The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman. The first part is scheduled for worldwide release on November 5, 2026, while the second part is set for Diwali 2027. The films will release in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam across India.
Sony Pictures will handle global distribution, excluding India, while Dharma Productions will distribute the film in the Hindi-speaking market. The film is also planned for a worldwide IMAX release.
